annotations.text:
CoreChoice — the full set

Settled: Lora for anything the app says, DM Sans for the interface. Considered palette as the default, Composed and Still in Settings.

Top row is the first-run path — test, profile, then a question. Bottom row is the answer path plus the two utility screens.

The advice text is real output from the working backend, so every layout is holding true content at true length.

Screen 1 — the promise in full

The two ticks are the whole conversion argument and they come BEFORE the first question, not after the last: your result is free permanently, and finishing adds five analyses.

Below them, the three things that decide whether a low-conscientiousness user finishes: you can stop anywhere, nothing leaves the phone, answer on instinct.

Screen 2 — three items at a time

Not five. At 390px with 44px targets, five Likert rows means scrolling mid-question, and scrolling is where people quit.

Progress is shown as '12 of 50' with a hairline bar. Honest about the length — hiding it would be the paywall move in a different costume.

Screen 3 — a position, not a quantity

Each trait is a dot on a line rather than a filled bar. A fill reads as 'how much you have out of the maximum', which is wrong for personality and nudges toward the same 'something is missing' feeling we removed from the verdict.

The five-analyses grant is confirmed here, on the screen where the promise is kept.

Screen 5 — one suggested, five listed

The suggestion carries its reasoning ('weighted five out of five, and you are asking about years'). A recommendation that explains itself is one people accept instead of re-deciding.

The other five are present and one tap away — never a grid of six.

Screen 7a is for you, not users

Four labels over the confidence the model already returns: Clear direction, Strong case, Slight edge, Genuinely close. Users never see a number.

'Strong case' rather than 'strong match' on purpose — it describes the argument the advisor made, not a fit with your personality. Nothing here claims to measure alignment, because nothing here does. A real alignment score would need its own schema field and a prompt change; worth doing deliberately if you want it, never by relabelling.

Screen 8 — prices are placeholders

[YOUR PRICES] — the tiers and the euro figures are illustrative until you set them against real Gemini cost. Measured: roughly 700 to 950 tokens per analysis.

'No subscription, nothing renews' is at the bottom deliberately. It is the sentence that answers the suspicion the whole category has earned.

For the build: the palette needs more tokens than three

These screens use about eight colours that are not in the nine-token set — border tints on wash boxes (#1F3A36, #2A514C), a dimmed accent for secondary text (#7FB8B2), and two ground steps below Surface (#0E1313, #161E1D).

They are used consistently, so they are a real extended palette rather than drift. Name them properly in the MAUI theme files — AccentLine, AccentDim, SurfaceSunken, LineSoft — so all three palettes define the same keys. Leaving them unnamed is how a fourth theme ends up half-styled later.
